common_name: Cream Carpet Lantana (Trailing Creamy Yellow Groundcover Lantana)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts after the last frost in well-drained, average soil in full sun; Cream Carpet's low, spreading habit makes it a strong choice for slopes, retaining walls, and large-scale groundcover plantings where mowing or frequent shearing is impractical.

directions: Cream Carpet is an older, widely grown trailing lantana selection dating to the late 1950s, prized for its dense mat of creamy yellow to soft white flower clusters that smother the low, spreading foliage from spring through frost. It stays under two feet tall while spreading several feet wide, rooting readily as trailing stems touch the soil, which makes it effective as a fast-covering groundcover on banks and in large beds. Like other lantana, it thrives in poor, well-drained soil and shrugs off heat, humidity, and drought once established, needing little supplemental water beyond an establishment period. In zone 8 and colder pockets of zone 9 it typically dies back to the crown after frost and regrows vigorously the following spring; in zones 10-11 it persists as a woody perennial.

common_name: Superbena Sparkling Amethyst Verbena (Purple-and-White Bicolor Spreading Verbena)

planting.note: Set out after the last frost in full sun with sharp drainage; the mounding-trailing habit makes this a strong spiller for mixed containers, hanging baskets, and landscape groundcover plantings.

directions: This Superbena series introduction bears large clusters of amethyst-purple flowers kissed with rosy-purple centers over dark green, powdery-mildew-resistant foliage, completely covering the plant without deadheading. Its mounding, trailing growth makes it an excellent spiller for combination containers and hanging baskets as well as a groundcover in beds. Grow in well-drained soil in full sun and allow the surface to dry between waterings, since it tolerates lean, dry conditions far better than soggy ones. Superbena selections are noted for vigorous heat, drought, and mildew tolerance, remaining floriferous through the hottest, most humid stretches of the Gulf Coast growing season.

common_name: Estrella Voodoo Star Verbena (Red-and-White Star-Patterned Spreading Verbena)

planting.note: Set out after the last frost in full sun with well-drained soil; the mounding, semi-trailing habit suits both landscape beds and combination containers.

directions: Part of the Estrella series, Voodoo Star produces showy clusters of red, star-shaped florets tipped with creamy white points, giving each cluster a distinctive bicolor, pinwheel-like pattern from late spring through mid-fall. The olive-green foliage forms a lush, mounding, semi-trailing habit that fills out containers and border edges without becoming leggy. It flowers heavily in full sun and tolerates heat and short dry spells well once established, though it benefits from consistent moisture during the hottest weeks of summer for the best bloom coverage. In zones outside its 9-11 perennial range it is grown as a heat-loving warm-season annual bedding plant.
